SpamWise privacy policy

Publication draft · Updated October 17, 2026

SpamWise is developed by Tim Morgan. For privacy questions or requests, contact tim@tim.codes. This page describes the current implementation; the app and this policy have not been published to the Mac App Store.

Mail and local storage

SpamWise reads selected mail and bounded mailbox pages through Apple Mail, with macOS Automation permission. It uses message text and metadata to suggest or apply Inbox, Review and Junk decisions. It does not delete mail or move it to Trash. Apple Mail continues to communicate with your configured mail providers under their own terms.

Settings, sender rules, decisions, correction examples, retry data, action records and spending records are stored on your Mac in SpamWise’s containers. Optional learning and reviewed-content retention can store additional bounded message text. Credentials are stored in Keychain. Portable backups are encrypted with a recovery key that you keep separately; they exclude credentials. Exports may contain personal mail information, depending on the export you choose. Keep those files private.

Contacts access is optional. When granted, SpamWise matches addresses locally to provide relationship evidence. It does not upload your address book as a list. Sender addresses and relationship evidence may still appear in a remote model request when you allow mail sharing.

Optional model providers

Cloud classification requires permission for the selected provider. The request can include sender information, subject, shortened message text, available evidence, your filtering preferences and selected correction examples. Enabled attachment text extraction and image OCR can add text to that context. Email can contain personal, confidential or sensitive information about you and other people. SpamWise sends requests directly to the selected provider using your API key; Tim Morgan does not operate a relay for these requests.

  • Anthropic Claude: the API’s commercial retention and training terms apply. Standard API inputs and outputs are generally deleted within 30 days, with documented exceptions. A zero-retention arrangement is separate; SpamWise does not enable or verify it. See Anthropic’s retention policy.
  • OpenAI: SpamWise uses the Responses API with store: false. This disables normal stored-response state, but does not itself disable abuse monitoring or every form of retention. OpenAI documents default abuse-monitoring retention of up to 30 days, with exceptions and eligible account controls. See OpenAI’s data controls.
  • Google Gemini: paid and unpaid service terms differ, with regional provisions. Unpaid-service terms permit model improvement and human review and instruct users not to submit personal or confidential information. Confirm which terms apply before enabling mail sharing; SpamWise cannot verify your project’s billing status or contractual terms. See Gemini’s terms.

Providers receive ordinary connection and account information such as your IP address and API authentication. The Claude SDK also sends app, SDK and operating system version information in its request header. Provider terms, account settings, retention exceptions and service locations govern their processing. Your provider may charge for requests separately from the free app.

You can revoke mail-sharing permission in Account settings. Revocation stops new requests; it cannot recall requests already sent or delete a provider’s records. Contact the provider for its deletion and account-control options.

On-device processing and optional evidence

The on-device model performs inference on the Mac when available. Explicit local mode also blocks SpamWise’s cloud providers and outbound evidence lookups. Merely selecting an on-device model does not turn off separately enabled evidence services. Local mode does not prevent Apple Mail or macOS from performing their own network operations. Private Cloud Compute is not an accepted production feature of this release.

Optional domain-age lookups send sender domains to IANA-discovered registration services. Optional Spamhaus reputation checks send sender/link domains through your selected DNS resolver or directly to Spamhaus over HTTPS. HTTPS uses your own query key stored in Keychain; mail bodies, full addresses and URL paths are not included. These checks are off by default, require acknowledgement of the selected service's terms and are blocked in local-only mode. Those services have separate terms. Optional Rspamd scanning sends bounded raw message data to a separately configured scanner at 127.0.0.1:11333. Its configuration determines any further processing, including outbound lookups. Both distributions support an explicitly selected local HTTP service; only direct builds offer external rspamc execution. Neither transport is enabled by default, and local-only mode blocks both. Image OCR and supported text attachment extraction run locally and do not load remote images or execute attachments.

Diagnostics, updates and your choices

SpamWise contains no advertising or tracking integration. Activity and usage statistics are local. A redacted diagnostics export omits keys and message content by default; inspect any file before sharing it. Emailing support sends your message and any attachments you choose to Tim Morgan through email services.

The direct-distribution variant supports a manual GitHub release check when a release repository is configured. That request exposes normal network information to GitHub, without mail content or provider credentials. The App Store variant does not include that updater. No release repository is currently configured.

Pause stops new processing. Dry run prevents mail actions but can still send authorized model requests. Quitting SpamWise stops its background monitor; disable the Mail extension separately when you want to stop extension callbacks as well. You can forget retained examples, remove rules, revoke permissions or remove the app’s stored data. See support and complete removal instructions. Removing the app alone leaves its data and Keychain credentials for reinstall.

This policy should be reviewed when data flows or provider terms change. The published version will carry its revision date here.
